action: General advice: treat unexpected texts asking for bank or card details as phishing; do not open the link, and contact your bank through its official channel.
date_note: Corrected 22 Nov: Kyodo (via Kumanichi) and Jiji (via Nippon.com) say the arrest was on 7 November and the referral to prosecutors on 9 November; the earlier date was ZATAZ's update day.
exec: Tokyo police referred to prosecutors a man arrested over a car-mounted fake mobile base station in Ginza that cut phones' service; the suspect denies it.
impact: The Star (relaying Japanese reporting) says more than 10,000 smartphones lost service; this is not a number of people defrauded.
plain: Police in Tokyo arrested a man over a fake mobile base station in a parked car in Ginza and sent his case to prosecutors. He denies it.
summary: Tokyo's Metropolitan Police Department arrested a 31-year-old Chinese national on 7 November over a fake mobile base station in a car parked in Ginza, Kyodo and Jiji report; on 9 November he was referred to prosecutors under the Radio Law, including interference with NTT Docomo's service. The Star says more than 10,000 smartphones lost service. The suspect denies the offence.
title: Tokyo: man arrested over fake base station said to have cut service to more than 10,000 phones

evidence.quote: caused more than 10,000 smartphones in the surrounding area to lose cellular service for about an hour.
Yu Hai, 31, a resident of Tokyo's Kita Ward

validation.note: Follow-up 22 Nov: Kyodo (Kumanichi) and Jiji (Nippon.com) each report the MPD arrest on 7 Nov and referral on 9 Nov. The more than 10,000 smartphones figure is from The Star only (ZATAZ gave more than 10,000 devices in under two hours). The police's own release was not read.

review.note: Title, 31-year-old Chinese national, 7 Nov arrest, 9 Nov referral, Radio Law/Docomo, denial, more than 10,000 phones figure and evidence quotes against Kumanichi, Nippon.com and The Star
